$schema-note: The fixed Event Runner admin identity (design brief §5.2; full spec docs/plans/2026-08-27-admin-identity-story.md part 6). Not a seventh preset: the admin obeys data-mode and ignores data-theme, so the generator emits this set ONCE PER MODE and never once per (theme, mode) pair. That emission rule is the mechanical statement of 'the admin ignores data-theme', and apps/web/src/lib/themeModes.test.js asserts it.
$palette-note: Channels are [r, g, b] numbers, never hex strings. The light ground is a warm-leaning grey pulled toward lead and proof stock, not a cool blue-grey: the distance from the generic dashboard slate is a stated design requirement (admin story part 5).
$palette-words-light: proof-stock grey, type-metal near-black, lead-grey rule, bench graphite, galley tint, oiled-steel focus, oxide alarm red, checked green, held caution amber, standing-matter grey
$palette-words-dark: night-side charcoal, cast-bone type, banked lead rule, lamp graphite, night galley tint, lit-steel focus, held oxide red, held green, held amber, dead-matter grey
$colors-note: Every entry resolves under :root[data-mode='light'] and :root[data-mode='dark']. Both values are authored; no dark value is derived from its light twin.

--admin-ground-rgb.$role: (a1) The room itself. The base page ground, tonal, never pure white or pure black.

--admin-ground-raised-rgb.$role: (a2) A region sitting above the room, reached by tint, not by shadow.

--admin-ground-proof-rgb.$role: (a3) The draft / unpublished-changes ground. The rough stock a proof is pulled on.

--admin-ground-input-rgb.$role: (a4) The ground inside a form control, distinct from both above so a field reads as a field without a heavy border.

--admin-ground-alarm-rgb.$role: (a5) The destructive and rejection ground. Low chroma; the words carry the weight.

--admin-ink-rgb.$role: (b1) Primary text. Type-metal near-black in light, cast bone in dark. Never pure black, never pure white.

--admin-ink-secondary-rgb.$role: (b2) Hints, metadata, and support text. 'Muted' never means 'below the bar'.

--admin-ink-data-rgb.$role: (b3) The mono role's ink, tuned so a dense mono column does not out-weigh the prose beside it.

--admin-ink-disabled-rgb.$role: (b5) Dead matter and disabled controls. Still readable.

--admin-ink-link-rgb.$role: (b6) The admin's own link colour, which is never the client accent.

--admin-rule-hairline-rgb.$role: (c1) Row, field, and region separators. The workhorse.

--admin-rule-strong-rgb.$role: (c2) Region and table-head boundaries. One per region.

--admin-rule-header-rgb.$role: (c3) The job line's rule, the heaviest rule in the room.

--admin-rule-alarm-rgb.$role: (c4) The rule around a destructive or rejected surface.

--admin-state-live-rgb.$role: (d1) Ink for the published state. Always paired with the word 'Live'.

--admin-state-draft-rgb.$role: (d2) Ink for the unpublished state; its ground is --admin-ground-proof-rgb. Always paired with the word 'Draft'.

--admin-state-error-rgb.$role: (d3) Ink for a rejection; its ground is --admin-ground-alarm-rgb.

--admin-state-caution-rgb.$role: (d4) Ink for a warning that is not a failure.

--admin-focus-ring-rgb.$role: (e1) One visible focus colour that clears both --admin-ground and --admin-ground-input in both modes. Never the client accent.

--admin-client-accent-ink-rgb.$role: (f2) The ink that reads on the accent, for the rare case the marker is filled behind a glyph.

$alias-note: (f1) The one client-owned colour, written from config/theme through buildRuntimeThemeCss like any other override. It defaults to the admin ink, so an unset accent renders as a plain ink marker rather than as nothing. The legibility floor lives in packages/shared/src/theme.cjs: when the resolved accent fails against --admin-ground in a mode, both slots fall back to --admin-ink and the editor says so.
$component-note: (f3, f4) Two component tokens, and only two, so the 'accent appears in exactly two places' rule is greppable. Any other reference to --admin-client-accent in apps/web fails review.
$scalar-note: (c) rules ship as a colour plus a width pair (brief §3.7). (e2) the focus offset keeps the ring off a hairline. (g) type and shape are fixed, never writable from config/theme.
$font-note: (g1, g2) Source Sans 3 carries everything a person reads as language. IBM Plex Mono carries everything the machine owns. No --admin-font-* token is ever writable from config/theme, so the generator always emits these two faces whatever preset a deployment runs.
